question.problem:
Given the system
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14249546/assets/0e89fc57b6af2ddf2a71246dbadc7feb8425d1e1e0ab8f988e7e8ad97d22cff7.svg)
which of the following statements are true?

I. The system is consistent dependent

II. The system has no solution

III. The system is consistent independent
question.worked_solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14249546/assets/3e3e8adb0d6e13f7d3b4c3e450b25a789480ac53189ab92385174688e460b2cc.svg)

Using Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -4 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14249546/assets/4122fb4ef56aa99161b15bc25001ca728a6cf7dae36d5dac0aac9b03dc411685.svg)

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
2x -3y= 4
$$

The basic variable is $x,$ and we have a free variable $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*.

As a result, only statement I is true.
